messages.subject: cannot open compressed file
parts:
Hi. I am having this problem. I am running a linux via virtual machine. r studio and r. I tried install.package (ggir, dependencies = T) and it didn't help. I tried to run it on a single file and changed the file name to different names still didn't work. my file is about 700 mg and the type is BIN.


Part 4
 1Error in readChar(con, 5L, useBytes = TRUE) : cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning message:
In readChar(con, 5L, useBytes = TRUE) :
  cannot open compressed file '/home/maher/gexit/output_gtest/meta/ms3.out/NA', probable reason 'No such file or directory'

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] cannot open compressed file
parts:
Hi Maher,

Did you fix this problem?
Usually these errors occurs when milestone data is moved and/or file paths are changed.
The best way to investigate is by starting with new input and output directory, and to process the data freshly file by file to better understand what file is causing the issue.

Also a mistake I sometimes make is that I look at the incorrect output directory, not realising that the actual action happens somewhere else in my laptop.

Best,
Vincent

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] cannot open compressed file
parts:
Hi Charles,

I see you have commented in several posts with similar issues. I think you are struggling to set up your directory and file paths in your scripts. I suggest you to take some time to revise that the directories and files are well specified in your paths in the GGIR script. Do not change any of the names of the folders produced by GGIR (for example, your output folder and everything that comes inside).

For example, the error described above is triggered when the output directory is not well defined in the GGIR script.

Hope this helps, otherwise let me know.

Best,
Jairo

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] cannot open compressed file
parts:
Hi Charles,

It's difficult to tell from here, that's why I suggested that you spend some time making sure all paths are correct. For example, I see your datadir and your outputdir are identical except for the begining (datadir = "D:/a Coortes Pelotas[...]", outputdir =  "D:/Coortes Pelotas[...]"). That might be right if your directories are organized like that, but it looks weird to me. Also, you have 2 consecutive quotes in studyname (in your script: studyname = ""#mystudy"), which might be producing errors when running the script.

Best,
Jairo
